thread.title: Bertelsmann CEO: EU's digital tax plan could hurt - MarketWatch

author: Zeke Turner
title: Bertelsmann CEO: EU's digital tax plan could hurt - MarketWatch
text:
BERLIN--New European tax plans targeting digital revenue could exacerbate the existing competition problems presented by American tech companies, Bertelsmann SE & Co. KGaA chief executive Thomas Rabe said Tuesday.
If Bertelsmann, Europe's biggest media company by revenue, had to also pay the charges on digital revenue, "I would find this quite inappropriate," Mr. Rabe said.
"We are paying direct taxes already...in all the countries where we operate," Mr. Rabe added. "We would be effectively taxed twice" in Europe, he said.
The new European tax charges, if passed into law later this year, would include an additional tax at 3% of revenue derived from certain digital activities by companies whose annual global revenue exceeds 750 million euros ($930.8 million).
On average, the European Union estimates that tech companies pay around 9.5% in tax on their profit on the continent compared with 23.2% for traditional industries, though tech lobbyists dispute that figure.
Bertelsmann in 2017 reported an effective income-tax rate of 30.8%.
"It's very clear that the playing field is not level," Mr. Rabe said, referring to the difference between taxes and regulation applying to his company--which makes money from areas such as book publishing, magazines, television and education--and American technology companies such as Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +4.03% Facebook Inc FB, +0.42% , Alphabet Inc.'s GOOG, +3.10% Google., Apple Inc. AAPL, +4.75% and Netflix Inc (NFLX).
Net profit for 2017 rose 5.4% to EUR1.2 billion compared with EUR1.14 billion a year earlier, while sales rose 1.4% on year to EUR17.2 billion, Bertelsmann said.
Digital revenue accounted for 46% of Bertelsmann's total sales.
